Splitting at one, applying theta reciprocity, and substituting x to 1/x produces a rational polar term plus an integral with symmetric s and 1-s exponents; exponential decay makes it entire. The formula continues zeta and exposes reflection. An entire reciprocal-gamma prefactor normalized at s=1 then shows zeta(s)-1/(s-1) is entire. Interpretation: self-duality makes continuation and symmetry consequences of one representation, while the rational term records theta's nondecaying constant mode. Boundary: initial interchange remains in sigma>1 and exact exponents are formula-sensitive.

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: theta Mellin representation on the critical line becomes a real even integral. Theta reciprocity gives phi'(0)=-1/2, decay handles infinity, and two integrations by parts transfer the frequency factor into phi''-phi. Adding one-half e^u makes a theta-derived Phi even without changing Phi''-Phi. Interpretation: completion moves from frequency multiplication to kernel differentiation, and reciprocity supplies the needed boundary cancellation. Boundary: this constructs a transform but proves no sign changes; glyphs and scales are OCR-sensitive.
